name: Chapter 17: Locomotion and Movement
description: Types of movement, muscles, sarcomere, sliding filament theory, human skeleton, joints and disorders

cards.definition:
Locomotion = voluntary movement that changes place
All locomotions are movements, but not all movements are locomotions

cards.term: Structure used for both feeding and locomotion in Paramoecium?
cards.definition: Cilia (move food through cytopharynx and help locomotion)

cards.term: Structure used for both prey capture and locomotion in Hydra?
cards.definition: Tentacles
Search of food, shelter, mate, breeding grounds, favourable climate, or to escape predators

cards.term: Three types of movement shown by human cells?
cards.definition: Amoeboid, ciliary, muscular

cards.term: Which human cells show amoeboid movement?
cards.definition: Macrophages and leucocytes
Pseudopodia formed by protoplasmic streaming; microfilaments are involved

cards.term: Two examples of ciliary movement in humans?
cards.definition: Cilia in the trachea remove dust; cilia move ova through the female reproductive tract
Swimming of spermatozoa, water current in sponge canals, locomotion of Euglena

cards.term: Locomotion needs coordination of which systems?
cards.definition: Muscular, skeletal and neural
Mesoderm

cards.term: What percentage of adult body weight is muscle?
cards.definition: 40–50%
Excitability, contractility, extensibility, elasticity

cards.term: Skeletal vs visceral vs cardiac muscle
cards.definition: Skeletal: Striated · voluntary · attached to bones; Visceral (smooth): Non-striated · involuntary · walls of hollow organs; Cardiac: Striated · involuntary · heart (branched)

cards.definition: Both striated. Skeletal: voluntary, unbranched. Cardiac: involuntary, branched.
Moving food through the digestive tract and gametes through the genital tract
A collagenous connective tissue layer, the fascia

cards.term: Plasma membrane and cytoplasm of a muscle fibre?
cards.definition: Sarcolemma and sarcoplasm

cards.term: Why is a muscle fibre a syncytium?
cards.definition: Its sarcoplasm has many nuclei

cards.term: Store house of calcium in a muscle fibre?
cards.definition: Sarcoplasmic reticulum

cards.term: Figure 17.1 · Cross section of a muscle
What gives skeletal muscle its striations?
cards.definition: Distribution of two proteins, actin and myosin, in alternate bands on myofibrils

cards.text: Light band = {{c1::I band (isotropic)}}, contains {{c2::actin}}. Dark band = {{c3::A band (anisotropic)}}, contains {{c4::myosin}}.

cards.term: Mnemonic for A and I bands?
cards.definition: dArk = A band; lIght = I band
Thin = actin. Thick = myosin.
An elastic fibre bisecting each I band; thin filaments attach to it
A thin fibrous membrane holding thick filaments together in the middle of the A band
Portion of a myofibril between two successive Z lines: the functional unit of contraction
Central part of the thick filaments not overlapped by thin filaments

cards.term: True or false: the H zone has both thick and thin filaments.
cards.definition: False. The H zone has only thick filaments.

cards.term: Anatomical vs functional unit of muscle?
cards.definition: Anatomical: muscle fibre. Functional: sarcomere.
Two F-actins helically wound; each F-actin is a polymer of G-actin monomers

cards.term: Two other proteins on the thin filament?
cards.definition: Tropomyosin (two filaments along F-actin) and troponin (at regular intervals on tropomyosin)

cards.term: What masks myosin-binding sites on actin at rest?
cards.definition: A subunit of troponin
Meromyosins
HMM: globular head + short arm. LMM: tail.
The HMM (head and short arm) projecting outward from the myosin filament at regular distance and angle

cards.term: Enzyme activity of the myosin head?
cards.definition: It is an ATPase, with binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin

cards.term: Figure 17.3 · Actin filament and myosin monomer

cards.definition: Filament: Actin: thin · Myosin: thick; Band: Actin: I band · Myosin: A band; Units: Actin: G-actin → F-actin · Myosin: meromyosin; Extra: Actin: troponin, tropomyosin · Myosin: ATPase head

advancedHtml.backHtml:
Actin vs myosin

Compare

FilamentActin: thin · Myosin: thick
BandActin: I band · Myosin: A band
UnitsActin: G-actin → F-actin · Myosin: meromyosin
ExtraActin: troponin, tropomyosin · Myosin: ATPase head

cards.definition: Contraction occurs by sliding of thin filaments over thick filaments
A motor neuron plus the muscle fibres connected to it
Junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma: the motor-end plate
Acetylcholine

1) Nerve signal → ACh → action potential in sarcolemma
2) Ca²⁺ released; Ca²⁺ binds troponin
3) Actin sites unmasked
4) Myosin head (ATP energy) binds
5) Cross bridge pulls actin to centre of A band
6) Sarcomere shortens

cards.term: During contraction, which bands shorten and which stay the same?
cards.definition: I band (and H zone) shorten; A band keeps its length
A new ATP binds to the myosin head
Ca²⁺ pumped back to the sarcoplasmic cisternae actin sites masked again Z lines return

cards.term: Why do dead bodies become stiff (rigor mortis)? (intuition)
cards.definition: With no ATP, myosin heads cannot detach from actin, so cross bridges stay locked
Lactic acid from anaerobic breakdown of glycogen after repeated activation
Myoglobin (red)

Red: much myoglobin, many mitochondria, aerobic
White: little myoglobin, few mitochondria, much sarcoplasmic reticulum, anaerobic

cards.term: Example: which fibres dominate in a flying bird's breast vs a chicken's breast?
cards.definition: Long-flying birds: red (endurance). Chicken breast: white (short bursts).

cards.text: In a muscle fibre, Ca²⁺ is stored in the {{c1::sarcoplasmic reticulum}}; the thin filament has two F-actins plus {{c2::tropomyosin}} and {{c3::troponin}}.

cards.definition: Bone: very hard (calcium salts). Cartilage: slightly pliable (chondroitin salts).

cards.term: Number of bones in the human skeleton?
cards.definition: 206 (plus a few cartilages)

cards.term: Number of bones in the axial skeleton?
cards.definition: 80
Skull, vertebral column, sternum, ribs

cards.term: Number of bones in the skull?
cards.definition: 22: 8 cranial + 14 facial

cards.text: The human cranium is made of {{c1::8}} bones; the face has {{c2::14}}.

cards.term: Where is the hyoid bone, and its shape?
cards.definition: A single U-shaped bone at the base of the buccal cavity
Malleus, incus, stapes (in each middle ear)

cards.term: Why is the human skull called dicondylic?
cards.definition: It articulates with the vertebral column by two occipital condyles

cards.term: Number of vertebrae in an adult?
cards.definition: 26

cards.term: What passes through the neural canal?
cards.definition: The spinal cord

cards.term: First vertebra, and what does it articulate with?
cards.definition: Atlas; with the occipital condyles

cards.text: Vertebral column: cervical {{c1::7}}, thoracic {{c2::12}}, lumbar {{c3::5}}, sacral {{c4::1 (fused)}}, coccygeal {{c5::1 (fused)}}.

cards.definition: "Breakfast at 7, lunch at 12, dinner at 5": cervical 7, thoracic 12, lumbar 5

cards.term: Number of cervical vertebrae in almost all mammals?
cards.definition: Seven, even in the giraffe and the whale
Protects the spinal cord, supports the head, gives attachment to ribs and back muscles
A flat bone on the ventral midline of the thorax
12
Each has two articulation surfaces on its dorsal end
First 7 pairs: attached dorsally to thoracic vertebrae and ventrally to the sternum by hyaline cartilage
8th, 9th, 10th pairs: join the 7th rib by hyaline cartilage, not the sternum directly
11th and 12th pairs: not connected ventrally
Thoracic vertebrae, ribs, sternum
Bones of the limbs and their girdles
30

cards.text: Fore limb: humerus, radius and ulna, carpals ({{c1::8}}), metacarpals ({{c2::5}}), phalanges ({{c3::14}}).
Hind limb: femur, tibia and fibula, tarsals ({{c1::7}}), metatarsals ({{c2::5}}), phalanges ({{c3::14}}), and patella.

cards.definition: Femur (thigh bone)
A cup-shaped bone covering the knee ventrally: the knee cap
Thumb has 2, each of the other four fingers has 3: 2 + 12
Articulate the limbs with the axial skeleton

cards.term: Each half of the pectoral girdle consists of?
cards.definition: A clavicle and a scapula
A large triangular flat bone in the dorsal thorax between the 2nd and 7th ribs
The flat expanded process of the scapula's spine; the clavicle articulates with it
A depression below the acromion that articulates with the head of the humerus (shoulder joint)
The clavicle: a long slender bone with two curvatures

cards.term: Figure 17.9 · Right pectoral girdle and upper arm

cards.definition: Two coxal bones

cards.term: Each coxal bone is formed by fusion of?
cards.definition: Ilium, ischium, pubis
The cavity at the fusion point of ilium, ischium and pubis, where the femur articulates
Ventral meeting of the two halves of the pelvic girdle, containing fibrous cartilage

cards.term: Figure 17.10 · Right pelvic girdle and lower limb

cards.definition: Bones per half: Pectoral: clavicle + scapula · Pelvic: coxal (ilium, ischium, pubis); Socket: Pectoral: glenoid cavity · Pelvic: acetabulum; Limb: Pectoral: fore limb · Pelvic: hind limb

cards.definition: Points of contact between bones, or between bones and cartilages; they act as a fulcrum
Fibrous, cartilaginous, synovial
No movement; sutures between flat skull bones
Limited movement; between adjacent vertebrae
A fluid-filled synovial cavity between the articulating surfaces; allows considerable movement

Ball and socket: Humerus and pectoral girdle (shoulder); femur and acetabulum; Hinge: Knee (also between phalanges); Pivot: Atlas and axis; Gliding: Between carpals; Saddle: Carpal and metacarpal of thumb

Low Ca²⁺ in body fluids → rapid spasms
Decreased estrogen levels (age-related)
Accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
